LESSON: AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.5: Auditory discrimination

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Auditory discrimination. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What sounds do different environment. whistles, phone ringing, hooting animals produce?

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Auditory discrimination helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

In this part you learn to Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Auditory discrimination”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Auditory discrimination is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Auditory discrimination”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Auditory discrimination to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Auditory discrimination from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Auditory discrimination: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Auditory discrimination?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.
